newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH ZLOTY INCHES HIGHER, FOREIGNERS SIDELINED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH ZLOTY INCHES HIGHER, FOREIGNERS SIDELINED.

text.p: The Polish zloty cautiosly headed upward against the currency basket amid wide spreads as foreign investors remained on the sidelines in early trade.

Dealers said a holiday in London would likely limit the role of foreigners in forex trade on Monday after their $350 million withdrawl from zloty instuments last week pushed the zloty down to all-time lows against the basket.
"Zloty weakening can not be expected but any gains are likely to be small...with nearly no oders from London or New York," said Piotr Czyzewski, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
At 0755 GMT the zloty was at 1.01/0.86 percent from the parity rate, stronger than opening's 0.68/0.35 percent and Friday's close at 0.64/0.50 percent.
It was at 3.1960/00 to the dollar up from opening's 3.2040/140 and at 1.8927/60 to the mark up from 1.9010/80.
Last week foreign investors sold Polish debt instruments in order to cut central European currency exposure after the Czech crown's decline in recent weeks.
But analysts said macroeconomic fundementals were better in Poland than in the Czech Republic, which would probably keep the zloty headed upward in the longer-term.
On the money market overnight rates fell below 21 percent as banks showed cash surpluses despite a 264 million zloty outflow on Monday, dealers said.
O/N rates were at 20.45/20.95 percent against opening's 21.45/21.65 percent while tomorrow/next straddled 21 percent at 20.80/21.10 after opening at 21.50/21.80 percent.
